issue.title: (Html)Helper not handling paths containing %, # and ? chars correctly

repository.name: cakephp
repository.description: CakePHP: The Rapid Development Framework for PHP - Official Repository

issue.body:
So while digging and testing some more regarding #2233, I've figured that the entity-encoded URLs seem to origin from `HtmlHelper::url()` and the percent-encoded ones from `Helper::_encodeUrl()`, and I've stumbled over problems with the `%`, `#` and `?` chars. I'm not quite sure whether CakePHP was ever ment to handle these chars properly though.

Let's assume we want to link to the following file: `/100%-balloonfishwool-jacket?.jpg` (I know, `?` is invalid on Windows). The `HtmlHelper::url()` method would produce the following URL:

```
/100%-balloonfishwool-jacket?.jpg
```

As you can see neither `%` nor `?` are encoded. The problem with this is that an unencoded `%` char can cause a `400` (Bad Request) response on some servers (try http://cakephp.org/100%-balloonfishwool-jacket.jpg), and that the unencoded `?` will of course act as the query string delimiter.

Now `Html::_encodeUrl()` on the other hand would produce the following URL:

```
/100%25-balloonfishwool-jacket?.jpg
```

The `%` char is encoded properly, but `?` is still unencoded.

Another problem with `Html::_encodeUrl()` and the `%` char appears in case it's followed by chars that would form a hex-digit. Say there were no hypens in the path, ie `/100%balloonfishwooljacket?.jpg`, then we would end up with:

```
/100%BAlloonfishwooljacket?.jpg
```

The `%` is not encoded anymore, as `%ba` was treated as a percent-encoded char.

Last but not least there's the `#` char, it's also not being encoded, and furthermore in `Html::_encodeUrl()` it causes the following chars to be treated as not part of the path (the same applies to `?`).

So while in `/100% balloonfishwool jacket?.jpg` the spaces and the `%` char are encoded correctly:

```
/100%25%20balloonfishwool%20jacket?.jpg
```

a path like `/#wtf/100% balloonfishwool jacket?.jpg` would result in:

```
/#wtf/100% balloonfishwool jacket?.jpg
```

Not even the spaces and the `%` char are encoded anymore.

As mentioned initially, I'm not 100% sure whether we should expect CakePHP to handle this correctly anyways, ie whether this is actually considered an issue?

Again this was tested against 2.4.2
